title: spec review: B1: planner_runs routing integration — taxonomy → router → tier per headless decision, mode off byte-identical, shadow Opus launch, hold instead of downgrade, telemetry rows and skip rows, re-escalation (P3, P5, P6, P9, P15, P17)
spec:
Why: planner_runs.run_group/launch_routed (planner_runs.py:1090-1236) launch every escalate-route decision on [models].planner (Fable); tick() drops routine/none points silently; run_group's same-state_version guard returns without a record; usage is logged only as bus.log_run planner_decision rows. The Wave A modules are merged on goal/T-0674 and need one integration point: planner_taxonomy.classify(point, ctx, *, goal, task); planner_router.load_cfg(pool_cfg), fable_reserve_ok(headroom_share, cfg), decide(classification, ctx, route, *, cfg, availability, evidence, jev_signal, sample), record(decision, *, subject, route, jev_signal, root), RouterDecision(tier, mode, hard, hold, hold_reason, reasons, hard_reasons, soft_score, shadow_tier, candidates, evidence, decision_type); planner_telemetry.record_launch/record_usage/snapshot/materiality/record_materiality/record_skip/read_invocations; jev_planner.should_ask/ask(..., state_version, task); planner_shadow.eligible/launch/parse/record/score (T-0729).
What (planner_runs.py, decision.py, goals.py; tests in tests/test_planner_runs_routing.py, existing tests keep passing):
- goals.launch_planner(repo_path, prompt, account_id, max_budget_usd, log_path, extra_env=None, model=None): model None keeps cfg["models"]["planner"]; the argv is otherwise unchanged.
- decision.route: kind "retrospective" -> routine "retrospective_deterministic"; ctx.get("state_unchanged") True -> none "unchanged_state" (checked right after the infra check). Existing tests unchanged.
- tick(): before routing each point, ctx["complexity"] = task complexity for held points else goal complexity; ctx["state_version"] = state_version(goal_id); ctx["state_unchanged"] = the _goal_launches guard's last_state_version equals it. classification = planner_taxonomy.classify(point, ctx, goal=goal, task=task). Every point that does not reach run_group records planner_telemetry.record_skip(goal_id=..., event="tick", reason=..., kind=..., payload_key=...) with reason routine, none:<route reason>, fix_round_in_flight, or unknown_gate.
- run_group(sections, pool): rcfg = planner_router.load_cfg(pool.cfg); the group's decision uses the section with the highest route (existing max) and its classification. availability = {rcfg["default_tier"]: {"available": bool(models alias configured) and account is not None, "reason"}, rcfg["escalation_tier"]: {...same...}, "fable_reserve_ok": planner_router.fable_reserve_ok(headroom_share, rcfg)} where headroom_share = None when the picked account's daily_budget is 0 else 1 - (day_tokens + planner_day_tokens) / daily_budget. evidence = planner_scorecard.class_evidence(models[default_tier], decision_type, band, task_class, architectural, root=STATE, cfg=pool.cfg) inside try/except (ImportError, Exception) -> {"n": 0, "noninferior": None, "reescalation_rate": 0.0}. hard_reasons = planner_router.hard_escalation(...); jev_signal = jev_planner.ask(...) only when jev_planner.should_ask(rcfg["mode"], rcfg["jev_mode"], hard_reasons, availability, route)[0], with state_version and the held task; sample = random.random(); decision = planner_router.decide(...); planner_router.record(decision, subject=goal_id, route=route, jev_signal=jev_signal). Re-escalation (P15): before deciding, if the goal's latest invocation row (planner_telemetry.read_invocations filtered by goal_id, max started_at) has tier == rcfg["default_tier"] and (classification decision_type == "architectural_replan" or "repeated_spec_rejection" in hard_reasons or "lineage_cap" in hard_reasons), set ctx["reescalation"] = True before hard_escalation/decide so the router forces the escalation tier.
- Effects of the decision: mode off -> launch_routed exactly as today (argv byte-identical, verified by test) and no shadow. decision.hold -> every section record gets status "held_for_fable", hold_reason = decision.hold_reason, notify.notify_once(goal_id, f"held_for_fable:{launch_id}", ...); return {"launched": False, "reason": decision.hold_reason}; the next tick retries. Otherwise launch_routed with route replaced by dataclasses.replace(route, tier=decision.tier) so the alias resolves through [models] (fable -> planner). Telemetry: before launching, before_snapshot = planner_telemetry.snapshot(goal_id); after launch planner_telemetry.record_launch(launch_id=..., goal_id, event="tick", decision_type, kind=the group's highest-route kind, payload_keys=[each section's payload_key for kind != held; for held sections the bare held task id], model=resolved model id, tier=decision.tier, account=account.id, complexity=ctx complexity, band, task_class, architectural, route=route.name, route_reason=route.reason, mode=rcfg["mode"], state_version, packet_chars=len(prompt), started_at, reescalation=bool(ctx.get("reescalation"))); store telemetry_before (the snapshot) and launch_started_at on the record. Shadow: ok, why = planner_shadow.eligible(decision, rcfg, sample=sample); when ok, planner_shadow.launch(prompt, model=models[decision.shadow_tier], account=the [[claude_accounts]] dict for account.id, budget_usd=limits.max_budget_usd.planner_shadow default 1.5, log=STATE/runs/f"planner-shadow-{goal_id}-{launch_id}.log") after the production launch; store shadow_pid/shadow_log/shadow_started_at on the record; any exception is printed to stderr and ignored.
- _record_decision_usage(r): additionally planner_telemetry.record_usage(launch_id, input_tokens=..., output_tokens=..., cache_read_tokens=..., cache_write_tokens=..., usd=..., latency_s=now - started_at, outcome=..., session_id=...) when the record has a launch_id.
- reconcile(): when a running record's process is gone and telemetry_before exists: planner_telemetry.record_materiality(launch_id, before, planner_telemetry.snapshot(goal_id)); when shadow_log exists and the shadow pid is gone (goals.identity_of False): parsed = planner_shadow.parse(shadow_log); planner_shadow.record(...); planner_shadow.score(row, that materiality) stored as shadow_agreement on the record.
Acceptance tests use the sandbox pattern of tests/test_planner_runs.py (patched launch_planner/Popen, no real subprocess).
acceptance: tests/test_planner_runs_routing.py::test_mode_off_argv_identical_to_legacy — with [planner.routing].mode off, run_group produces exactly the argv the pre-change code produced for the same decision (captured via patched Popen, compared list-equal), no shadow Popen call, and no held_for_fable record

tests/test_planner_runs_routing.py::test_shadow_mode_launches_fable_then_opus_shadow_without_bus_writes — shadow mode: the first Popen argv uses models.planner and .mcp.planner.json, a second Popen argv uses models.opus, .mcp.planner-shadow.json and --disallowedTools; bus task files and plan.md are byte-identical after the shadow launch; the record carries shadow_log and a launch row exists with tier fable, mode shadow and packet_chars

tests/test_planner_runs_routing.py::test_hard_decision_holds_when_fable_unavailable — active mode, goal complexity 9, escalation tier unavailable (models.planner missing or pool.pick None for the planner role after the default-tier check): no Popen call, every section record has status held_for_fable with hold_reason starting fable_unavailable, one notify_once, and the next tick retries instead of giving up

tests/test_planner_runs_routing.py::test_skips_and_usage_and_materiality_rows — a routine point and an unchanged-state goal produce planner_skips rows with reasons routine and none:unchanged_state; a launched decision followed by a fake exit whose log carries usage yields usage and materiality rows merged under the same launch_id, materiality naming the task created during the run

tests/test_planner_runs_routing.py::test_reescalation_forces_fable_after_opus_and_decision_row — a goal whose latest invocation row has tier opus and whose held point has spec_review_request_changes 2 launches on models.planner in active mode with reescalation True in the launch row, and decision_log.explain(goal) shows a planner_route row whose hard_constraints contain repeated_spec_rejection and reescalation; tests/test_decision.py::test_retrospective_and_unchanged_state_routes — kind retrospective routes routine retrospective_deterministic and state_unchanged True routes none unchanged_state

risks.issue: should_ask(router_mode, jev_mode, hard_reasons, availability, route) compares route with `route != "escalate"` (a plain string equality), but the spec's run_group prose reuses the same bare word "route" for both this call and planner_router.decide(classification, ctx, route, ...), which accepts the Route dataclass/dict via a `_get()` helper. If the executor passes the Route object (as decide/hard_escalation expect) instead of route.name into should_ask, the comparison is always False, should_ask always returns (False, "deterministic"), and jev_planner.ask is never invoked in any mode — silently disabling the P12 shadow signal. No acceptance test exercises jev_planner.ask/should_ask at all, so this regression ships undetected.

Spec asks launch_planner(repo_path, prompt, account_id, max_budget_usd, log_path, extra_env=None, model=None) to add a model param, but the "Effects of the decision" section keeps run_group calling the existing launch_routed (planner_runs.py:1090) unmodified, which only calls goals.launch_planner(ROOT, prompt, account.id, budget, log) positionally (no model) when the resolved tier is the default planner alias, and hand-builds a separate duplicate argv for every other tier without ever calling goals.launch_planner. The new model kwarg therefore has no caller anywhere in the described data flow and no acceptance test references it — either dead code the executor adds for no reason, or a missing step where launch_routed's duplicated argv-building (lines 1096-1109) was meant to be replaced by a goals.launch_planner(model=...) delegate.

tick() currently builds groups[goal_id].append((point, ctx, route)) as 3-tuples, and run_group unpacks 3-tuples throughout (e.g. `for point, ctx, section_route in sections`, and `route = max((section[2] for section in sections), key=...)` which only extracts the Route objects, discarding which point/ctx/classification produced the winner). The spec requires per-point classification from planner_taxonomy.classify computed in tick(), then says run_group's decision uses 'the section with the highest route (existing max) and its classification' and mutates that winning section's ctx for reescalation — but never states the sections tuple grows to 4 elements, never lists the several unpack sites in run_group needing updates, and doesn't resolve what happens when two bundled sections tie on route priority (max() silently picks whichever appears first in iteration order, so telemetry/reescalation would attribute to an arbitrary section, and the losing section's classification is dropped entirely).

planner_telemetry.py already does `from . import STATE, bus, planner_runs, pool, scorecard` (used at orchestrator/planner_telemetry.py:307 inside interactive_by_goal). The spec now has planner_runs.py import planner_telemetry to call record_launch/record_usage/snapshot/record_materiality/record_skip/read_invocations, creating a two-way circular import between the two modules. It will likely work if planner_runs.py imports via `from . import planner_telemetry` (module reference, resolved lazily) since neither module touches the other's attributes at top-level import time today, but the spec doesn't say this explicitly, and an executor writing `from .planner_telemetry import record_launch` (attribute import) would hit an ImportError depending on which module happens to import first across the package's various entry points (daemon.py, cli.py, etc.).

planner_shadow.launch() returns {pid, log, stderr_log, argv} with no pid_start, but the spec's reconcile() step calls goals.identity_of(shadow_pid, ...) to detect a finished shadow run. Without a captured shadow_pid_start, identity_of degrades to a pure liveness check (os.kill(pid, 0)) with no protection against the shadow pid being reused by an unrelated process before reconcile() notices it exited — unlike production launches, which always carry pid_start. The spec's field list ('store shadow_pid/shadow_log/shadow_started_at') should either add shadow_pid_start (requiring planner_shadow.launch to capture one via goals._proc_start) or explicitly accept the weaker liveness-only check for shadow runs.

suggested_spec_changes: State explicitly that jev_planner.should_ask's `route` argument must be route.name (the plain string), not the Route object, to avoid silently disabling the jev shadow signal.

Add one acceptance test that asserts jev_planner.ask is actually invoked (with correct args) on an active/shadow-mode escalate decision that clears should_ask's gates, since none of the five listed tests exercise that path.
Either drop the goals.launch_planner model=None parameter from scope, or specify the call site in launch_routed (or elsewhere) that is supposed to use it, plus an acceptance test covering it.

Specify the sections data structure run_group receives from tick() (tuple arity, and which section's classification/ctx is authoritative when a bundled group ties on route priority) rather than leaving the tuple shape to be inferred.
Note that planner_runs.py must import planner_telemetry via `from . import planner_telemetry` (not `from .planner_telemetry import ...`) given the existing planner_telemetry -> planner_runs import.
